This week
Awards rose to 76 this week from 58, and EPC items to 142 from 117, but the money went to a few hands. MCC took the two largest metals awards: the US$195m Vinmetal steelmaking package in Vietnam and US$120m of bauxite mining works at Sanmenxia. Voith Hydro won both Slovak pump-turbine and motor-generator packages, and Alstom Ferroviaria took Italian signalling. For a bidder, the pattern is that head contracts are going to integrated contractors and equipment makers. The realistic opening is a subcontract or supply position under them, not the main contract.
— World Trade Pro Research

Shipping, ports & logistics
Latam Cargo to increase flower exports with Bogota terminal expansion
freightwaves.com
What it means: Latam is building and financing a new cargo terminal at El Dorado in Bogotá, adding air cargo capacity for Colombian flower exporters and their forwarders.
Oil, gas & LNG · Strait of Hormuz
Crude Is Back at 80% in the Gulf, but Refined Products Are Stuck at 35%
oilprice.com
What it means: Gulf crude exports are back to 80% to 85% of pre-war levels but refined products are stuck at 35%, so product buyers face tighter supply than crude buyers.
Shipping, ports & logistics
Tanker Market Surged in October
hellenicshippingnews.com
What it means: Record VLCC rates in October pushed Suezmax and Aframax rates higher, so charterers of dirty tankers paid more in every size class.
Oil, gas & LNG · Strait of Hormuz
Iraq’s Oil Production Soars to 2019 High as Hormuz Flows Surge
oilprice.com
What it means: Iraq produced 4.6 million bpd in October, its highest since 2019, which means more crude available to buyers and more tanker demand out of the Gulf.
